title: Heterogeneous kernel sampler and dwell-time reclaimer for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As tenant mixes and prompt shapes diversify, a one-size kernel selection and time-based eviction leads to unnecessary decode stalls and suboptimal GPU utilization. Paged KV causes fragments with different dwell characteristics; some fragments are hot briefly, others persist. Existing allocators react on occupancy heuristics and prefill windows but miss cross-tenant kernel heterogeneity and short-lived hot prefixes.

Goal: Implement a small-footprint kernel sampler that tracks short-term kernel performance by fragment class (sequence-length profile + tenant weight) and combine that with a dwell-time reclaimer that schedules eviction passes at safe micro-windows to reduce fragmentation and reduce prefill-induced decode interruptions. Target improves median and p95 prefill latency for multi-tenant bursts while reducing wasted token-cost by reclaiming low-value fragments before aggressive compaction.

Scope:
- Kernel sampler: lightweight probabilistic sampling per-serving-kernel to estimate per-fragment decode throughput and tail latency for common sequence-length buckets. No per-request instrumentation heavy path.
- Dwell-time reclaimer: maintain approximate dwell histograms per KV shard; use these to rank candidate fragments for on-demand reclamation and to create short reclaim windows aligned with decode waves.
- Integrate sampler signals with the scheduler so kernel selection prefers kernels with low tail for current seq-length distribution and can pre-warm compatible kernels during prefill.
- Ensure fully feature-flagged rollout, telemetry hooks, and a traffic-safe canary (A/B) with automatic rollback on regressions.

Non-goals: full per-fragment ML predictor, radical rewrite of allocator, or tenant-weight rebalancing in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel sampler running behind feature flag with <5% overhead on CPU for sampler bookkeeping.
Prefill latency p95 reduced by >=15% on simulated multi-tenant burst workload (bench dashboard).
Observed reduction in cross-shard decode stalls during compaction windows in canary by >=20%.
Eviction passes reclaim low-dwell fragments with false-positive rate <10% as measured in unit-level simulator and integration test.
All changes behind feature flags and deployed with canary + automatic rollback policy.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampler weight decay, per-bucket aggregates, and reclaimer ranking.
Simulator run using tenant-mix traces (prod-snapshot-2026-01) to validate reclaim precision and effect on stall metrics.
End-to-end canary in Dedicated pool with 2% traffic and synthetic burst profiles; collect p50/p95 prefill latency, tail decode stalls, and token cost delta.
Long-run 24-hour soak test to measure sampler stability and drift under changing seq-length distributions.
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in main branch; smoke CI run.
Deploy sampler-only mode (no scheduler influence) to staging for 48h validation.
Enable scheduler integration in staging and run synthetic burst test suite.
Canary in production Dedicated cluster at 2% for 6 hours; evaluate dashboard thresholds. If pass, ramp 10% for 24h, then 50% for 24h, then global.
If any regression >5% in p95 prefill or >3% regression in tail decode stalls, auto-roll back via rollout manager.
comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after perf retro; initial design doc linked. Assigned to Liam.
2026-02-20 Liam Chen: Spike done — sampler prototype shows 3% CPU overhead and useful per-bucket latency differentiation. Posted spike notes in Confluence.
2026-02-26 Design review: PM (Nora Singh) asked for explicit rollback thresholds; added to rollout_plan. Security reviewed and OK with low risk (no secrets).
2026-03-02 Eng sync: Decided to keep sampler state sharded by KV shard id to avoid cross-shard coordination; reduces coordination overhead at cost of slightly noisier estimates. Trade-off accepted.

2026-03-05 PR opened: runtime#4823. Early review feedback from Marco: prefer exponential decay with capped counters instead of sliding windows to simplify memory. Action: switch to EMA + count-backed shrink.
2026-03-09 Integration test: Staging canary shows 12% p95 improvement for 128/256 seq-length heavy traces; small regressions on very long seqs (2%) — investigating kernel warmup path.
2026-03-10 Liam Chen: Marked In Progress. Next: implement kernel pre-warm hook timed by sampler prediction and add scoreboard to detect prefill-interleaved compaction.
